basis: Deafness, cataracts and neurodevelopmental impairment/polyneuropathy define the syndrome. Subcutaneous calcification lacks evidence of functional damage.
Brain calcification with cognitive and motor impairment; isolated ANA positivity does not establish immune-mediated disease.
Disease of the vestibular labyrinth of the inner ear.
Adenomatous neoplasm originating in colonic or rectal mucosa.
Congenital anterior segment dysgenesis with corneal opacity and visual loss; additional characteristic abnormalities are ocular.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy in 30/30; hypotonia and motor dysfunction reflect neurologic disease.
Corynebacterial infection directly produces chronic skin ulceration.
Inherited adrenal steroidogenesis defect; no additional common directly damaged organ established.
Suppurative infection of the middle ear.
An isolated neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Arthropod-transmitted viral infection umbrella; specific organ damage varies substantially between infections.
Locally aggressive neoplasm originating in bone; distant involvement is uncommon.
Carcinoma originating in the renal medulla. Sickle cell trait is an association, not blood involvement caused by the carcinoma.
Obesity supports the metabolic axis; sparse syndrome information. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Renal bicarbonate wasting causes metabolic acidosis; characteristic cataracts, glaucoma and keratopathy. Intellectual disability in 3/3 supports neurologic involvement.
Inherited predisposition specifically targets colorectal neoplasia; this label does not imply that cancer is already present.
Benign neoplasm originating in the urinary bladder, included in the renal axis.
Severe neurodevelopmental disease with structural brain abnormalities; fixed joint contractures in 5/6 (~83%) establish musculoskeletal involvement.
Cutaneous sweat duct obstruction with characteristic skin lesions.
Necrotizing bacterial infection of soft tissues, encompassing skin/subcutis, fascia and muscle; tissue depth varies across forms.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with pyramidal involvement; progressive distal muscle atrophy and foot deformity are characteristic and common (>30%).
Defined as disease of the endocrine system; additional organ damage is subtype-dependent.
Inherited metabolic syndrome with renal dysfunction and cholestasis; arthrogryposis in 80–99%. Platelet, skin and CNS abnormalities (30–79%) omitted at cap.
Disordered porphyrin metabolism; cutaneous, neurologic and hepatic manifestations vary by subtype and are not universal across the umbrella.
Infection-induced encephalitis with encephalopathy in 8/8; cataracts in 2/2 assessed support ocular involvement. Respiratory signs lack evidence of direct lung damage.
